newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi defends Italy's drive to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi defends Italy's drive to join EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi defended Italy's capacity to join a European single currency on Tuesday, saying negative remarks from some of its partners were inspired by "fear" of the dynamism of Italian industry.

He made his hard-hitting remarks to reporters shortly before French President Jacques Chirac said that Italy may not be among the first group of countries to join a European monetary and economic union in 1999.

"I can assure you that we will take a leading role and I can assure you that some of these observations about the currency also stem from the great fear that the dynamism of Italian industry produces among competitors in other countries," Prodi told reporters at an environmental meeting in Rome.
"We aren't the only ones who fear French and German competition. The French and the Germans are also very much afraid of Italian competition," he said.
"If we remain united as a country I'm telling you that we'll astound them," he said.
